I realize this is a very open question, and I don't expect an answer with a ton of detail, but do the mods make record of various plans/strategic moves/advancements that countries make, and if so, to what extent? To explain my motivation a bit, I realize that to a fair degree gameplay here is allowed to be somewhat detached from reality, but not completely. I really want to have a good grasp of what (within the realm of non-reality) is considered reasonable and what is "absurdly absurd."

Our best examples are found in the "On Realism" post.

Essentially things can only be unreasonable if you can not reason them.

Mongolia's Mechanical horses are an often used example.

It was initially unreasonable because they came into existence overnight with no funding or development.

A while later is was perfectly reasonable because he explained how they worked, used news posts to update progress on their development, and had trade to explain the funding.

Realism is a tool to help ensure far gameplay.

"The sky is the limit" is not quite accurate here, because if you can reason and explain how you went beyond it, there is no real limit.

Also consider the level of effect actions have on other players. I believe someone had a news post about wormholes not too long ago. We allowed this with the stipulation it not be used an attempt to justify further actions. "I got these soldiers from the wormhole, I discovered this science from the wormhole, etc" would not be okay. Using it for humor or developing back story is fine.

I think once we unveil our first crisis event and explain it you'll get a better picture of our goals. In the future we would like to test players' creativity by asking them to react to unrealistic scenarios in realistic manners, as well as rewarding those who go the extra mile in these situations.

You'll also find that allowing things sometimes as humorous and unexpected consequences.

Brazil discovered Atlantis, which was fine given the same stipulation as wormholes. It has neither population or resources. Finding ancient technology there would be unfair to other players, so it was perfectly allowed.

Then, a player actually claimed it.

This too was okay because it is an unpopulated under water city.

However the player tried to form units. This was unreasonable because he had neither workers nor resources.

Another nation has offered to help him, and that's okay because it's actually not much different than a player assisting a small real-life nation. It's possible and reasonable.

So an Atlantic fleet is perfectly reasonable as long as it is created in a way that is fair to other players. They have to prove they got resources and workers, and acquired it over a period of time that makes sense.
